title: The Pigeon Finds a Hot Dog!
author: Mo Willems

hero.name: Pigeon

hero.source_note: Named Mo Willems character — source from Teachers Pay Teachers or Creative Fabrica for Pigeon clip art

ambiguous.issue: Could be possessive pronoun or a digging mine
ambiguous.reason: Book centres on Pigeon claiming ownership of the hot dog — possessive meaning is correct

ambiguous.issue: Could map to a question mark symbol or a person asking — abstract concept
ambiguous.reason: The Duckling's persistent questioning is a key story element; a question mark icon is most recognisable

notes: The Duckling is a secondary named character who needs a sourced PNG — ideally matching Mo Willems' art style (yellow duckling with similar simple design). Core story tension is possession and persuasion: Pigeon finds the hot dog and Duckling wants a taste. Words like 'mine', 'share', 'give', and 'question' capture this dynamic well for AAC use. 'Yummy' is highly motivating and frequently modelled during read-alouds. 'Napkin' appears in the story as Duckling uses one to taste the hot dog. Ketchup, mustard, and bun are already in activity_images so they do not need to be added to fringe slots but can be referenced as supplementary vocabulary on a second board if desired.
